A_e2_unit_defects.finding_summary: All six records carry a vitamin-A unit string that exists on NO other vitamin-A row in the 15,414-record frozen corpus: `mg RAE` occurs on exactly 3 rows (223563, 223572, 328644) and `mcg DFE` on exactly 3 rows (231334, 231335, 263865). The vocabulary actually in use for vitamin A is `mcg RAE` (299 rows), `mcg` (889), `IU` (830), `mg` (16). The six rows under review are the entire population of the anomaly, so this is a bounded transcription defect class, not a pipeline behaviour.

D_folate_residuals.source_finding: The Bulk 1340 printed Supplement Facts panel has TWO value columns - `4 Heaping Scoops (360 g) in Water` and `4 Heaping Scoops (360 g) in 2% Milk`. The folate row prints `667 mcg DFE 167%` in column 1 and `725 mcg DFE 181%` in column 2, each with its own folic-acid child (`400 mcg` water / `435 mcg` milk). The DFE total is the parent; the folic acid is a form breakdown already inside that total; the two columns are alternative preparation bases, not addends.

D_folate_residuals.engineering_consequence: The representations are now sourced. The remaining work is one reviewed dose-safety reconciliation change (owner: dose-safety/folate), specified exactly, not a source question: (a) recognise the declared-total row by exposure basis / DFE unit rather than by a parent-name vocabulary that omits the name `Folic Acid`; (b) treat a nested form row of the same canonical nutrient as part of the declared total even when it is a subset; (c) never sum quantities that belong to different serving bases - pair them by basis and take the maximum labelled basis for exposure. Fixtures for the change: 201420, 243808, 246430 (all three currently unreconciled), with 228823 (passes at 1.95% against the existing ~2% tolerance) as the guard. Owners already exist: test_folate_dose_basis_reconciliation.py, test_dose_safety_shared_contract.py.
